# Fixtures

Committed API responses, captured live and used as both test input and evidence for the claims in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §2–3.

**Read-only.** Nothing in this directory is generated by the build or modified by tests. If a fixture needs to change, recapture it with the commands below and note the new date.

**Captured:** 2026-09-09 / 2026-09-10
**Licence:** Open Parliament Licence. Not covered by the repository's MIT licence.

---

## Contents

| Path | Source | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `lords-full/page-0001.json` … `page-0041.json` | Full Lords register, all 815 members, `includeDeleted=true` | ~9 MB |
| `commons-full/page-0000.json` … `page-0180.json` | All 193 Commons Category 7 records | ~370 KB |
| `categories-lords.json` | `/Categories?Type=Lords` | 3 KB |
| `registers.json` | `/Registers?Skip=0&Take=5` | 3 KB |
| `commons-820/PublishedInterest-Category_*.csv` | Register 820 CSV export, extracted from ZIP | ~1.6 MB |
| `commons-updates.zip` | `registerUpdatesDocument` — misnamed, is a PDF | 167 KB |

---

## What each one proves

**`lords-full/`** — the workhorse. 815 distinct members across 41 pages.

- `page-0001.json` and `page-0002.json` differ, while `page-0000.json` (not committed) was byte-identical to page 1. This is the evidence that **`page` is 1-indexed despite the API documenting "default 0"**. A 0-indexed loop silently drops the last 15 peers.
- `page-0001.json` contains **Lord Agnew of Oulton (id 4689)** — dense shareholdings across both category schemes, migration timestamps, a duplicate correction pair (ids 30972/30973), and cessation text variants. Most parser tests should use him.
- Deleted interests reach back to **2010**, with `deletedWhen` populated.
- Category IDs `1002`–`1005` (current) and `4`/`12`/`31` (retired) are disjoint: the retired categories contain **zero live records**.

**`commons-full/`** — 193 records, 10 pages.

- The `fields` array is **typed and structured** — `OrganisationName`, `EndDate`, `ShareholdingThreshold` and so on. No text parsing required, unlike the Lords.
- Only **11 of 193** have a populated `EndDate`.
- **Zero** records have a `parentInterestId`, so `ExpandChildInterests=True` is precautionary rather than necessary.
- Threshold split: **155 at 15% of issued share capital, 38 at over £70,000**.
- Only **3 of 193** mention "plc".

**`categories-lords.json`** — requested with `Type=Lords`, returned all 12 Commons categories with `"type":"Commons"` and a self-link reading `Type=Commons`. Proves the Interests API is **Commons-only** and the `Type` parameter is silently ignored.

**`registers.json`** — 50 registers total, roughly fortnightly. IDs are **non-sequential** (820, 812, 804, 803, 801), so order by `publishedDate` rather than id. Shows the `csv`, `registerDocument` and `registerUpdatesDocument` link shapes.

**`commons-820/`** — extracted from the ZIP returned by `/api/v1/Interests/csv?registerId=820`. Despite the route ending in `csv`, the response is a ZIP containing one CSV per category. `PublishedInterest-Category_7.csv` has the dynamic fields **already flattened into named columns**, which makes this a better ingest path than the JSON API. Note `updatedDates[]` becomes `Updated_1` and `Updated_2`.

**`commons-updates.zip`** — misnamed deliberately, kept as evidence. The first bytes are `25 50 44 46` (`%PDF-1.7`), so the updates document is a PDF and not machine-readable. Do not attempt to parse it; the CSV snapshots carry the same information.

## Verified figures

Every count in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §2–3 comes from these queries. Reproducible against the committed fixtures.

```powershell
$f = (Get-ChildItem lords-full\*.json).FullName
$c = (Get-ChildItem commons-full\*.json).FullName
```

| Figure | Value | Query |
|---|---|---|
| Lords members | 815 | `jq -s '[.[].items[].value.member.id] \| {rows: length, distinct: (unique\|length)}' $f` |
| Shareholdings, current scheme | 2,558 total / 2,136 live | `jq -s '[.[].items[].value.interestCategories[]? \| select(.id >= 1002 and .id <= 1005) \| .interests[]?] \| {total: length, live: ([.[] \| select(.deletedWhen == null)] \| length)}' $f` |
| Shareholdings, retired scheme | 2,864 total / 0 live | same with `select(.id == 4 or .id == 12 or .id == 31)` |
| Category 2(d) records | 66 | `jq -s '[.[].items[].value.interestCategories[]? \| select(.id == 1005) \| .interests[]?] \| length' $f` |
| Deletions at `2025-04-05T00:00:00` | 3,856 | `jq -s --arg d "2025-04-05T00:00:00" '[.[].items[].value.interestCategories[]?.interests[]? \| select(.deletedWhen == $d)] \| length' $f` |
| …of which shareholdings | **0** | same, plus `select(.id == 4 or .id == 12 or .id == 31)` on the category |
| Live records with cessation text | 77 of 2,136 | `jq -s --arg p "interest ceased" '[... \| select(.interest \| test($p))] \| length' $f` |
| Commons records | 193 | `jq -s '[.[].items[].id] \| {rows: length, distinct: (unique\|length)}' $c` |
| Commons `EndDate` populated | 11 | `jq -s --arg n EndDate '[.[].items[].fields[] \| select(.name == $n)] \| {total: length, populated: ([.[] \| select(.value != null)] \| length)}' $c` |
| Commons mentioning "plc" | 3 | `jq -s --arg n OrganisationName --arg re plc '[.[].items[].fields[] \| select(.name == $n) \| .value \| ascii_downcase] \| map(select(test($re))) \| length' $c` |

Note on quoting: PowerShell strips embedded double quotes when passing arguments to native executables. Pass string literals with `--arg` rather than inlining them in the filter.

## Recapture

Run from this directory. Takes about two minutes.

```powershell
# Lords — 41 pages, 1-indexed
mkdir lords-full -Force | Out-Null
for ($page = 1; $page -le 41; $page++) {
    $out = "lords-full\page-{0:D4}.json" -f $page
    curl.exe -s -o $out "https://members-api.parliament.uk/api/LordsInterests/Register?page=$page&includeDeleted=true"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
}

# Commons — 10 pages, Take caps at 20 regardless
mkdir commons-full -Force | Out-Null
for ($skip = 0; $skip -lt 193; $skip += 20) {
    $out = "commons-full\page-{0:D4}.json" -f $skip
    curl.exe -s -o $out "https://interests-api.parliament.uk/api/v1/Interests?CategoryId=8&ExpandChildInterests=True&Take=20&Skip=$skip"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
}

# Supporting
curl.exe -s -o categories-lords.json "https://interests-api.parliament.uk/api/v1/Categories?Type=Lords&Skip=0&Take=20"
curl.exe -s -o registers.json "https://interests-api.parliament.uk/api/v1/Registers?Skip=0&Take=5"
curl.exe -s -o commons-820.zip "https://interests-api.parliament.uk/api/v1/Interests/csv?registerId=820"
Expand-Archive commons-820.zip -DestinationPath commons-820 -Force
```

**Always verify coverage after recapturing:**

```powershell
jq -s '[.[].items[].value.member.id] | {rows: length, distinct: (unique|length)}' (Get-ChildItem lords-full\*.json).FullName
```

`rows` and `distinct` must be equal. If they differ, pagination has failed and the capture is incomplete.

---

## Staleness

These are a snapshot. If Parliament changes a response shape, the fixtures become a record of how the API *used to* look, and the test suite will keep passing while production breaks.

That is why `CLAUDE.md` says to **stop and report** when a live response differs from `ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 rather than adapting the parser. A mismatch means either the API changed or the request is wrong, and both need a human.

Worth recapturing and re-verifying the figures above periodically — and certainly after any Parliament announcement about the registers.
